data.title: Final demand before seizure – broadcasting fee (suspicious)
data.summary: A letter claiming to be from the "Rundfunk-Beitragsservice Zahlungszentrale" demands €254.35 in broadcasting fee arrears within 48 hours of receipt. It threatens seizure and has several strong scam indicators, including a Lithuanian IBAN.
data.explanation: This letter demands €254.35 within 48 hours and threatens account and wage seizure. It looks like a scam. The payment account is Lithuanian, the sender is not your known Beitragsservice Musterstadt, and it tells you not to contact the usual office. The 48-hour deadline is also unusual for a real authority. Don't pay yet. Check your fee account directly with the official Beitragsservice, using contact details you already know and not those in this letter. If you're unsure, consider consumer advice or the police.

items.consequence: The letter threatens seizure (Zwangsvollstreckung) and extra costs of at least €180; this is likely a scam threat.
items.quote: Sie werden hiermit letztmalig aufgefordert den Gesamtbetrag innerhalb von 48

warnings: The payee IBAN is Lithuanian (LT), which is not plausible for a German broadcasting fee authority.
The payee is 'Beitragsinkasso UAB' (a Lithuanian company form), not the known Beitragsservice Musterstadt.
The letter demands payment within 48 hours and threatens seizure without further notice, which is typical scam pressure.
It tells you not to contact the known Beitragsservice address and to use only an e-mail address.
The salutation is faulty ('Sehr geehrte Herr') and the signature is oddly spaced, suggesting a forged letter.
